we observe most models are unable to be profitable, tending to fall into adversarial client traps or under-staffing
The agent operates a company over a one-year simulated horizon, starting with $200,000 in funds.
The episode terminates when funds drop below zero (bankruptcy) or the horizon ends.
which we mathematically formalize as a Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (POMDP)
Each task belongs to one of four industry domains
If the agent fails to complete a task by its deadline, it incurs a penalty of 35% of the advertised reward and a prestige reduction
higher prestige unlocks higher-reward tasks and linearly scales their payout
The company has a fixed roster of staff members that cannot be hired or fired.
The monthly payroll therefore grows monotonically with the number of completed tasks, creating pressure to prioritize high-reward tasks that outpace rising costs.
higher trust reduces the work required on future tasks from that client and unlocks higher-tier tasks
completing a task for one client slightly decays trust with all others
A subset of clients are adversarial: after the agent accepts one of their tasks, the environment inflates the work quantity, making the deadline nearly impossible to meet.
Adversarial status is hidden and never revealed directly.
adversarial clients offer competitively high rewards, so the agent cannot simply filter by price
The key hidden quantity is client reliability levels, which must be inferred from the pattern of task outcomes.
At the start of each turn, the agent receives a structured status summary containing the current timestamp, funds, monthly payroll, runway estimate, active task count
Calling sim resume advances the clock to the next scheduled event, typically a task checkpoint (25%, 50%, 75%, or 100% completion), a monthly payroll deduction, or the horizon end.
Work progresses only during business hours (weekdays), and payroll is deducted on the first business day of each month.
The agent's conversation history is truncated to the most recent K turns (we use K=20 in our experiments).
The scratchpad is the agent's sole mechanism for retaining information across context truncation
Each model is evaluated on 3 seeds using the default preset, for a total of 36 LLM runs.
We evaluate 12 models spanning seven providers
We compare against a greedy baseline that, in each turn, accepts the highest-reward task available on the market, assigns all employees to it, and advances the simulation clock.

YC-Bench is open-source and works with any LiteLLM-compatible model.
The benchmark uses the medium preset by default (moderate deadline pressure, 200 market tasks, 8 employees).
